chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

There is no hadd against one upon whom no hadd applies. The explanation of that is: if an insane person were to accuse a man of fornication, nothing would be due from him; so if a man were to accuse him in return, no hadd would be due against him.

key_terms.تَفْسِيرُ: the explanation or clarification of the ruling
key_terms.شَيْءٌ: anything legally due or applicable in consequence
key_terms.مَجْنُونًا: an insane person who is not legally accountable

ai.seo_question: Is the hadd for false accusation applied when the accused person is not legally accountable, such as an insane person?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the hadd for false accusation. It states that one who is not legally subject to hadd—such as an insane person—does not trigger the retaliatory application of hadd if another person accuses him in return.
